$comment: Facts about the Codex (ChatGPT) coding harness that relay's math depends on, extracted with REA 6.7.0 from @openai/codex 0.163.0 (linux-x64). Every entry carries `evidence`: how it was established. Kinds: observed (REA process capture of the real binary), static (string in the binary's .rodata, file offset given), documented (OpenAI docs, URL given), community (unofficial, unverified), prior (our assumption, to be calibrated).

codex app-server generate-json-schema --experimental (the binary emits its own protocol schema)
codex debug models (the binary emits its bundled model catalog)

models.observedContextWindowEvidence: observed: token_count.info.model_context_window = 475000 (= 500000 × 95%) in 4 232 rollout readings of gpt-6.1-sol on three plans from 2026-10-14T07:15Z on; 258400 in the 66 readings before that instant. pricing.$comment: Credits per 1M tokens at Standard speed, input / cached input / output. Reasoning tokens are output tokens. Codex has no separate cache-write charge.

speedMultipliers.$comment: Relative to Standard. `included` applies to subscription usage limits; `credits` to purchased credits / pay-as-you-go. The catalog describes the Fast tier as '2x speed, increased usage' (astra, sol 6.1) and '1.5x speed' (sol 6, luna; fast is their default_service_tier).

messagesPerFiveHoursPlus.$comment: OpenAI's own estimate of local messages per 5-hour period on Plus / Standard Business; an ordering check for the credit weights.

extendedContext.$comment: community: requests above 272,000 input tokens are priced at 2x input (matches catalog max_context_window 872000 vs context_window 272000)

rateAliases.$comment: Models without published rates, priced as another model. codex-auto-review (the automatic approval reviewer, 903 readings on one machine) has no published rate; at gpt-6.1-sol rates its usage fits the weekly meter within the rounding noise (weight fit 1.7, weakly identified: 111 credits in 29 points).

includedMeterWeight.$comment: What one published-rate credit of a model moves a subscription usage window, relative to gpt-6.1-sol. Fitted on the self_serve_business_prolite weekly window: 29 integer-percent steps over two windows (2026-10-19 → 10-22), cumulative credits per model at the published rates as regressors, non-negative least squares; residual SD 0.19 points (0.64 with a single rate). gpt-6-sol 0.94 ≈ 1 (window 1 only); gpt-6-astra 0.43–0.57 (5 steps, 254 credits); gpt-6-luna unidentified (5 credits in the data) and kept at 1. Purchased credits (metering 'credits') are charged at the published rates unweighted.
includedMeterWeight.evidence: observed: evidence/live/readings.json (3 623 prolite readings), the fit in harness/FINDINGS.md §9

windowsByPlan.$comment: documented: Plus and Standard Business limits are estimated per five-hour period plus a weekly limit; Pro plans currently have no five-hour limit; Enterprise/Edu flexible pricing has no fixed limits (credits). Durations in minutes are what the backend reports in windowDurationMins / window_minutes. Observed in rollouts and app-server probes (evidence/RESULTS.md §B–C): pro = primary 10080 min, no secondary (1 219 readings); team = primary 300 + secondary 10080 (444 readings); self_serve_business_prolite = primary 10080 min, no secondary (3 623 readings and the live probe); limit_id codex (premium seen on 3 team readings without windows).
windowsByPlan.evidence: documented: https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/pricing; static: status-line items five-hour-limit, weekly-limit at .rodata 0x0e6d6097

purchasedResets.effect: restores both the 5-hour and the weekly usage immediately; pulls the weekly allowance forward (no extra usage); the new weekly period starts at the first request after the reset; Plus and Pro personal accounts only; cannot be banked

clientNudges.note: the TUI itself proposes switching to a cheaper model when approaching limits; memory generation is gated at 25% remaining

observedSemantics.usedPercent: an integer (the schema's int32); on a weekly window it moved one point per ≈ 65 published-rate credits of gpt-6.1-sol work on self_serve_business_prolite, so nine small runs (10.3 credits) left it unchanged
observedSemantics.resetsAt: while a window is unused (0%) resets_at slides with the clock (now + window length, re-sent on every reading); the 7-day clock starts at the first metered use and resets_at then stays fixed; a reset mid-window (observed 2026-10-20 08:32Z, 5% → 0% with a new resets_at) shows up as a changed resets_at, which is what readers should key on
observedSemantics.staleReadings: readings of concurrent threads interleave, each carrying the snapshot its last response returned, so a pooled timeline shows 5 → 4 → 5; readers keep a high-water mark per window (lib/calibration.mjs capacitySamples)
observedSemantics.credits: self_serve_business_prolite: credits { hasCredits: false, unlimited: false, balance: null } with one 'Full reset' rate-limit reset credit available

capacityMeasured.$comment: Credits at the published rates (gpt-6.1-sol mix, included-metering weights applied) that fill 100% of a window: the ratio estimator 100 ΣΔC/ΣΔU over the account's pooled credit timeline (lib/calibration.mjs accountTimeline + capacitySamples), per plan as the rollouts on one machine saw it. Usage outside those rollouts (another device, the web) is invisible to it and biases the estimate low.

primary.credits: ≈ 6 300 (two windows: 6 353 over 5 points, 6 489 over 24 points, single-rate fit; see FINDINGS §9)
primary.confidence: good: 29 points, 1 937 credits, residual SD 0.64 points

Observed null for every thread on self_serve_business_prolite (0.163.0): the processor returns None when the backend's /wham/usage/thread_usage/query answers 403 or 404 (app-server/src/request_processors/account_processor.rs:1332-1372), so plans without purchasable credits expose no per-thread credit estimate and the published rates are the only per-thread price (evidence/RESULTS.md §C)
